name: FuriosaAI Warboy
memory_bandwidth_basis: Vendor-published: 66 GB/s DRAM bandwidth (FuriosaAI developer docs). LPDDR4x at 4266 MT/s.

flops.notes: 64 TOPS INT8 dense. Peak performance figure from FuriosaAI developer documentation.

notes: REAL VENDOR: FuriosaAI (furiosa.ai, Seoul, South Korea). Set to 'asic-other' because the schema enum does not include 'furiosaai'. Warboy is FuriosaAI's Gen 1 Vision NPU, built on Samsung 14nm with 5 billion transistors on a 180mm^2 die at 2GHz clock. 64 TOPS INT8, 66 GB/s LPDDR4x, PCIe Gen4 8x. The chip is designed for vision AI workloads — object detection, segmentation, classification — at the edge and in the datacenter. FuriosaAI SDK compiles TFLite and ONNX models for the Warboy NPU. The company has shipped two silicon generations: Warboy (Samsung 14nm, 2021) and RNGD ('Renegade', TSMC 5nm, mass production January 2026). A third generation co-developed with Broadcom (2nm compute die, HBM4/4E) was announced in May 2026 but is not yet in production. Warboy is NOT an LLM serving chip — it is a vision NPU. The successor RNGD targets LLM inference with higher compute and HBM. Process node is Samsung 14nm (not TSMC). TDP is 40W for the PCIe card.
